category: Google Drive link-to-direct-download generator, with API and folder packaging

free_tier.stated: Generating a link is free and needs no account: 'Paste your Google Drive link and generate a high-speed direct download link instantly. No account linking needed.' No price, byte allowance or account quota is printed anywhere on the page.
free_tier.notes: The product withholds its own numbers entirely; the quota it moves is Google Drive's.

per_object_cap.stated: Not stated. Nothing on the page names a size for a wrapped file or for the ZIP a folder share produces.
per_object_cap.notes: The page's own figures (4.2 GB, 1.8 GB) are mocked-up dashboard filenames, not limits, and are not used here.

retention.stated: Not stated. The wrapper stores a Drive file id, so the link lives as long as the Drive object does.

egress.terms: Every download is proxied through HubCloud as a 'high-speed direct download link'; folder shares are 'Download folders as ZIP archives instantly'. Nothing is metered and no allowance is printed.

interface_detail: REST upload endpoint `curl -X POST api.hubcloud.foo/upload`, announced as 'New: API v2.0 Released', with a dashboard at hubcloud.foo/drive/admin. The page also offers a 'Pack Manager' that combines several links into one package and a Drive integration that requires no account linking.
tooling: No client library. The generation step is a form on the page; the API is a single documented POST. Third parties already automate it: hubcloud.cfd is a public 'HubCloud Bypass' page whose only feature is 'Extract direct download links from HubCloud video/drive pages instantly'.
chaining: The middle layer of the Indian index chain: an index site posts a HubCloud link, HubCloud re-exposes the Google Drive file as a direct link that indexers and apps can hand to a downloader, and the same file is often re-wrapped one layer down by DriveSeed or GDFlix.

limits.value: unstated by HubCloud; the underlying Google Drive per-file download throttle is what a client hits

limits_note: The absence is the finding: a service whose product is removing somebody else's limit publishes no limit of its own, so a client cannot budget against it. The Drive-side ceiling is documented one link further down the chain by DriveSeed, which lists '403: User Rate Limit Exceeded - Fixed to Great Extent' as a release note.
binding_note: At 1 TiB a month the throttle that reappears is Google's per-file and per-session shaping on the Drive object behind the wrapper. HubCloud adds no counter of its own, so nothing else on this record can bind.

identity_cost.detail: Generating a link needs nothing: 'No account linking needed'. A dashboard exists at /drive/admin for managing files, but the public path does not require it.

reliability_note: Hubcloud.ink answered an empty 204; and the live host was reached only through hubcloud.foo, which redirects to hubcloud.ist. A client that hard-codes a host breaks within weeks.
confidence_note: Feature list, API endpoint and dashboard path were read on the live page. The absence of any published quota is itself documented. What would raise the rung: one measured download through a generated link, with the byte count and the status of the first throttle.

evidence.proved: live service at hubcloud.ist: 'Paste your Google Drive link and generate a high-speed direct download link instantly. No account linking needed.', 'New: API v2.0 Released', folder-to-ZIP share, Pack Manager
the same page served directly, confirming the redirect target is the app rather than a parking page
third parties run a dedicated bypass front for the service ('Extract direct download links from HubCloud video/drive pages instantly'), which shows the wrapper is used at volume

notes: The record prices a link wrapper, not storage: nothing here can be mounted, and the bytes always belong to Google. hubcloud.xyz was the ledger's assumed host and is dead.

extras.empty_hosts: hubcloud.ink (origin answered 204 with an empty body)
